nodes.label: Industry trends research (wearables, AI coaching, subscriptions, routing tech, running culture)
nodes.rationale: 40 verified findings; three most consequential: platform squeeze, unowned route-generation hero feature with cheap stack, Gen Z running boom.

nodes.label: Finding: route-generation whitespace is real and unowned
nodes.rationale: Training apps prescribe workouts without location intelligence; routing apps plan static routes without training context; nobody generates the run itself. Enabling stack (OSM routing, free elevation and weather, on-device AI) is nearly zero marginal cost, so the moat is personalization and execution.

nodes.label: Finding: platform giants commoditize generic AI coaching
nodes.rationale: Garmin Connect+ ($6.99/mo) and Apple Workout Buddy (motivational, not prescriptive) raise the bar; differentiation must be what they do not do.

nodes.label: Risk: Garmin Connect Developer Program paused to new applicants
nodes.rationale: HealthKit remains fully open (validates iOS-first) but Garmin integration is a launch risk.

edges.rationale: Evidence for hypothesis H2: no incumbent solves constraint-based adaptive route generation.
Supports H2; final verdict lands in Phase 4.
Generic AI coaching is commoditized; the route wedge is the defensible differentiation.
Wearable integration scope for the MVP must account for Garmin API unavailability.
